style.text: Open most balanced hands non-vul with 12 HCP, but could pass a bad one vul.
style.reading: with the rule of 20, min_hcp 13 vulnerable passes only the 4-3-3-3 twelves; a 'bad' twelve by honour quality is not expressible

style.text: Open balanced 11 usually only NV and only if especially good (aces, tens).
style.reading: judgment by aces and tens; under the rule of 20 no balanced eleven opens here

style.text: Unbalanced hands loosely follow the rule of 20, but use judgment based on honor location, spots, vul, and likely rebid problems.
style.reading: the judgment is not placed

style.text: If you have (say) stiff Q, don't count that for both 2 HCP and distribution!
style.reading: no predicate discounts a short honour in the rule of 20

style.text: Might pass borderline hands if judgment is that they'll be easier to describe later.
style.reading: judgment

style.text: 3rd seat can open light, especially if you want that lead
style.placed: open.third_seat_min 10 with a five-card suit (default; the notes give no number)
style.reading: 'want that lead' is not placed

style.text: Frequently respond light to opening bid, esp non vul
style.reading: no field for the response minimum: responses start at 6 HCP (card: 'Frequently respond with <6 HCP')

style.text: Routinely open 1N with 5-card major. 6-card m is possible, but never 'too good' a hand.
style.reading: 'never too good' is not placed

style.text: 2-level opening should be 6-card suit in 1st/2nd.
style.reading: five-card weak twos in 3rd/4th seat are implied, with no length stated: not placed

style.text: 'Good suit' = 2 of top 3. 'Good hand' = 8-10.
style.reading: Ogust's definitions (the compiler's Ogust answers have no such settings); used for variants[1] and variants[2]

style.text: Fourth seat 2-level opening shows a maximum weak 2 bid - definitely less than a solid 1-level opening
style.reading: a maximum read as the notes' 'good hand' (8-10)

style.text: 3-level opening should be a 7-card suit with 4-6 playing tricks if non-vul, and 6-7 playing tricks if vul.
style.reading: playing tricks have no predicate; 6-7 tricks on seven cards read as two of the top three honours, which also applies to weak twos vulnerable ('Sound Vul' on the WBF card)

style.text: At imps, we play 1st seat FAVORABLE preempt can be VERY light - almost any hand with a 6-card suit would 'qualify'. At matchpoints, we do NOT do this.
style.placed: variants[3]: first seat, favourable, IMPs: three-level openings on six cards, 0-10 HCP, any quality
style.reading: the card says 3x openings ('Jxxxxx and out possible'); weak_quality 0 also frees the weak twos in that seat

style.text: Do not preempt if your hand is too good (even if partner is a PH) or has too many 'flaws', such as good playability in side majors (especially spades) or too much stuff in your short suits. Ideally, you should really want the lead in the suit you preempt in.
style.placed: open.weak_other_major_max 3 (a weak two in a major has at most three of the other major)
style.reading: side-major length for three-level preempts and minor-suit weak twos, values in short suits, 'too good' and 'want the lead' are not placed

style.text: Gambling 3NT: no outside A or K if 1st-3rd seat.
style.placed: open.three_nt gambling: solid seven-card minor and no outside ace or king, in every seat
style.reading: outside values in 4th seat are not placed

style.text: 1N overcall is a good 15-18 HCP.
Fourth seat (sandwich) NT is 15-18 HCP.
style.reading: the compiler does not cover action after both opponents have bid

style.text: Balancing 1N is 11-14 vs. 1m; 11-16 vs. 1M.
Balancing JUMP 2N overcall is 19-21 HCP.
style.reading: no balancing 2NT in the compiled balancing seat

style.text: Double then 1N (or non-jump to 2N) by doubler is 18+-20 HCP
style.reading: the doubler's rebid is not compiled

style.text: Double then jump to 2N by doubler is 21-22 HCP
style.reading: the doubler's rebid is not compiled

style.text: Balancing double then 1N (or non-jump to 2N) is 15-18 HCP (17-18 after 1M)
style.placed: comp.strong_double_min 18 less comp.balance 3: a balancing strong double from 15
style.reading: the rebid is not compiled

style.text: Overcalls are wide range - 7-17 HCP.
style.reading: the card prints '8 to 16 HCP (usually)', inside the notes' extremes; the notes are taken

style.text: Balancing jump overcall is INTERMEDIATE - about an opening bid with 6-card suit
style.placed: comp.balancing_jumps true: balancing jumps are intermediate, 12-16 with six cards at the two level

style.text: If advancer bids a suit at the 3-level, this shows values (about 7-10 HCP)
style.reading: the compiler covers action over one-level openings only

style.text: Balancing double can be a king light
style.source: notes (they open at the 2-level and at the 3-level)
style.reading: over two- and three-level openings: not compiled

style.text: Double is Take-out. Advancer should bid game with 9+ HCP
style.reading: the compiler covers action over one-level openings only

style.text: Double tends to be for T.O. Advancer usually needs a six-card suit or 5-5 to go to the 5-level
style.reading: the compiler covers action over one-level openings only

style.text: Frequently respond with <6 HCP.
style.reading: no number: no field for the response minimum

style.text: VERY LIGHT: Openings, 3rd Hand, Overcalls, Preempts (none ticked)
1st seat favorable at IMPS 3x opening very light - Jxxxxx and out possible
Simple overcall: 1 level 8 to 16 HCP (usually)
Major opening, expected minimum length: 5 in 1st/2nd, 4 in 3rd/4th
